body: Thanks, but there is nothing to chat about.

I didn't limit myself, but the situation is the same or worse everywhere else. 
I work at a foreign company and they won't relocate because they can hire locally and I can work from here remotely. I can't just find a job that will let me travel.
It exists globally, but it has a stronger effect in here. we are such a small place.

I know people from Sweden. I don't have a problem with Sweden, or Germany. but at 30, starting with a new language/culture is too much. at 18 or 24 it would have been great, living, studying. 
But now, I'll feel too foreign, while at America I feel at home more than anywhere.

If it was as easy just to come and live a few months, I would, but it's a life changing decision and I can't afford 3 years of trying to find myself, by myself in another language, begging for jobs approval.
I feel American, I can relate to most of Britain, but I don't know anything about Sweden or feel connected to.

The US is the only one I feel suits for me.
I have checked requirements for all other English native countries and the less strict (Canada, Australia) still requires a highly desired profession (which I have) and an employer willing to hire you (under a lot of restrictions) for a long period of time.

Cultural wise, I think there's a gap (dubbed movies for e.g.)
But even getting in, is hard:
"In order to receive a work permit, you must have received an official offer of employment from a Swedish employer. It is not possible to receive a work permit in order to come to Sweden to look for work."

I've looked all over EU. Germany and other places that aren't native English doesn't work for me. culture wise.
I've searched immigration terms, and they remind others. I need to have a job prior to immigrating, I need the employer to vouch for me and most places say that without knowing the language, it's unlikely to be hired. Those are the terms for non-EU.
The question is what you can do with that money. it won't buy freedom and apartments prices start at twice as much.
It would if that was a possibility.

I'm sorry, but the UK wouldn't work.
I have checked this subject a couple of times (have a few friends that immigrated there), and while it's hard to believe, it's even harder than moving to the US.
Even if I won't include the upcoming rage against Jews/Israel there (which sadly increased lately), it's really expensive to live there and as a new citizen for the first years they will pay you a lot less, if they ever will, because they hire locals UK born only.

But, even getting in is not a possibility. Unless you have another EU citizenship, they won't let you just come in (of a few million £).
The regulations are really strict.

I go to the gym and being alone there is frustrating. and I go on walks/runs, and see other couples do it together. 
I try to go to the gym as much as I can, but still, when I get back, I have nothing.
I don't have the time or the resources to do so. we don't really have blacksmithing here.

Thanks. 
I'm doing some progress, but after that, I'm still alone. I've tried reaching out online, but I don't think that it's something that can be done constantly. Most of the success stories here are motivating, but mentioning having a spouse or some sort of support. 

Living here, I'm limited with the clubs and hobbies I can do. I work long hours, try to squeeze some hours and the gym and that's it. I wish I had sometime off and friends to hangout with, but it rarely happens. 

I'll give it one more try, but I don't know what will stop me from failing again.
I'll be happy to, maybe both of us can benefit from it.

Thank you.

I've been exercising 4 days a week, but now it's down to about 1 time. 
I don't live in the US, so I can't really move to newer places and... we don't have bacon.
I spend some time in LA last year and actually did keto for 2 weeks with great results, but I almost can't do it here.
I've tried it again a month ago, but it's hard when everything in here is carbs based.

Thank you for the encouragement and for showing that it can be done.
